keyFindings: The larger cloud pods deliver extremely cushioned, protective rearfoot cushioning rather than a soft or bouncy sensation
The significant rocker geometry produces a rolling ride rather than a bouncing one, making it smooth for steady-pace efforts
Despite its maximalist build, the shoe offers mild flexibility and pop at toe-off, handling strides and slight uptempo efforts without problems
Stability comes from bilateral sidewalls and forward guidance in the midsole rather than traditional stability features
Best suited as a long-run and daily training shoe for mileage-focused sessions rather than pace-driven workouts
Delivers a smooth, well-cushioned ride with a lively sense of rebound — softer than previous On models without feeling dense or unstable
Aggressive rocker combined with Speedboard plate creates dynamic forward propulsion, performing well at varied paces though not optimized as a speed shoe
The midsole provides stable, substantial cushioning suitable for daily training and long distances, though the minimalist upper offers reduced ankle support at faster efforts
Lighter runners may struggle to fully compress the CloudTec pods, while heavier runners risk bottoming out the suspension
Best suited as a recovery and easy-day trainer for runners prioritizing comfort over performance demands
Helion foam is the softest On shoe yet — finally delivering genuine cushioned comfort rather than the firm, hard sensation of earlier On models
Individual cloud pod compression and release creates a bouncy, enjoyable ride with an exaggerated forefoot rocker for snappy toe-off
Excels as a daily trainer and long-run shoe but struggles at faster efforts — weight becomes noticeable at tempo paces
Runs narrow with a shallow toebox; most runners should size up, and quality issues including peeling welded tape and insole compression after extended mileage are notable drawbacks
